card.hook: Here's the funny thing about Diocletian's Palace: you can wander around inside it all day and never see it, because you're standing in it. To get the big picture, you have to climb out.
card.stand_here: Stand on the terrace at Prva Vidilica, the first viewpoint on Marjan hill, and face east. It's a roughly 15-minute walk up stairs and paths from the old town, so you're looking back over the palace walls and terracotta roofs, with the harbour and the Riva in front.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the walls, roofs and harbour all in one shot. If your phone has zoom 2x or 5x, try it for a closer look at the roofs and walls. Use zoom 0.5x only if you want the terrace railing in the foreground.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the walls and roofs on the lower third, so the harbour and sky fill the rest.
card.best_time: One photography guide recommends sunrise for the eastern light on the city. It's also usually quieter up here than at the sunset spots higher up the hill.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera and hold your phone a little higher than your face. Try zoom 0.5x to fit more of the scene, and turn so the old town is over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: The Prva Vidilica terrace is an open public viewpoint. Some individual sights inside the palace may be ticketed, so check the official site before you go. The route up is stairs and paths, so wear comfy shoes.
card.challenge: Take the same photo twice, once from up here and once down on the Riva, and see which one makes the palace look bigger.
card.good_to_know: Emperor Diocletian built the palace at the end of the third century AD as his retirement home. Today it makes up around half of Split's old town, and people still live, work and eat inside its walls. UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage Site in 1979.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the terrace at Prva Vidilica, the first viewpoint on Marjan hill, and face east. It's a roughly 15-minute walk up stairs and paths from the old town, so you're looking back over the palace walls and terracotta roofs, with the harbour and the Riva in front.

card.hook: Bačvice never sits still: swimmers splashing, games in the shallows, people strolling the edge of the bay. The trick is to stop being part of the crowd and watch it from above.
card.stand_here: Stand in Hatzeov perivoj, the beach park on the road above the sand, and grab one of the shaded benches. Face south-west, with the beach lying below you.
card.zoom: Start at 0.5x to fit the whole curve of the bay, then switch to 1x for a more natural look. Try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out swimmers or the far shoreline.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and put the waterline along the lower third, then tap the water and drag the slider to make it a little darker so the bright sea and sand don't wash out.
card.best_time: Earlier or later in the day usually gives you softer light than at midday.
card.selfie_here: Use the raised walkway around the bay in Hatzeov perivoj: switch to the front camera, hold your phone at arm's length, and keep the beach and sea behind you. For a splashier shot, the shallow water in front of the sandy part of the beach is another option, with the beach behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: There's a protected swimming area and a lifeguard on duty at Bačvice. The rocky western end (Pomoraca Park) involves some climbing and isn't a formal lookout, so take care there.
card.challenge: Keep a tree branch or the park edge at one side of your frame, then find the one swimmer who looks like they're having the most fun.
card.good_to_know: Bačvice is Split's busy town beach, a sandy bay with the open Adriatic in front and the city behind. Hatzeov perivoj is the beach's own address, so it's a handy name to search for. Building work around the bay can sometimes creep into the view, so check your frame before you shoot. Wipe your camera glass first, because sea air and sunscreen smear it fast.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Hatzeov perivoj, the beach park on the road above the sand, and grab one of the shaded benches. Face south-west, with the beach lying below you.

card.hook: Walk to the end of Split's seafront and you'll see a big, dark green hill sitting over the pale town like a cozy hat. That's Marjan, and it's the easiest hill in Split to spot.
card.stand_here: Stand at the western end of the Riva, the seafront promenade, and face west. Marjan is the large wooded hill straight ahead of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole waterfront with the hill behind it. Then try 1x for a natural view, and 2x or 5x (higher zooms depend on your phone) to fill the frame with pine slopes.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the hill's ridge line on the top third and the promenade or water on the bottom third, then tap the hill and slide it a little darker so the sky doesn't wash out and the pines stay deep green.
card.best_time: Morning to early afternoon is usually the safest bet, because the sun is behind or beside you and lights up the hill. Late in the day the sun sets behind Marjan, so expect a darker, backlit shot.
card.selfie_here: For a hill-behind-you selfie, try the pebbly shore of Kašjuni Beach on the south side of Marjan, with the pine-covered slope rising over your shoulder. Use the front camera, and switch to 0.5x if your phone offers it, so more of the hill fits in.
card.rules_and_safety: The Riva is a busy, open promenade, so take a few frames, then step aside to check them instead of stopping in the walkway. Be aware of your surroundings, especially during peak tourist season.
card.challenge: Count how many shades of green you can fit between the ridge line and the water. Bonus points if you keep the horizon dead level.
card.good_to_know: Marjan is about 178 m high and covered in dense Mediterranean pine forest. Split people love it for weekend walks, jogging and beaches. Diocletian's palace stood a short walk away, and the emperor laid out the nearer slopes as a park, so it has been a park for a very long time. Over the last century and a half it has become a symbol of Split.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the western end of the Riva, the seafront promenade, and face west. Marjan is the large wooded hill straight ahead of you.

card.hook: Most spots make you pick one thing to photograph. The Riva hands you palm trees, a honey-coloured palace wall and a harbour full of boats all at once. It's almost unfair.
card.stand_here: Start in the middle of Trg Republike, the square at the west end of the Riva, and face into the square so the buildings frame both sides. Then walk the 200 m or so along the promenade, with the Riva to the south-east, and turn back to shoot the palms and palace wall from near the water's edge.
card.zoom: Use zoom 0.5x in the square to fit in the buildings on both sides. On the Riva, switch to 1x for the palms and the palace wall. Zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) is handy for picking out boats and strollers.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines at the square, stand on the centre line and keep the buildings level on both sides, and the photo almost composes itself.
card.best_time: Go near sunset if you want the Matejuška fishermen's harbour, where boats and strolling silhouettes are lit from behind. For the square and the palace wall, earlier or later in the day is kinder than harsh midday light.
card.selfie_here: Pose in front of the row of palm trees along the Riva (or on a bench beneath them) with your front camera, so the tall palms stay in the frame behind you. For a souvenir shot, try the big red SPLIT letters at the east end of the Riva near the cruise dock, but you may only get part of the Riva behind you there.
card.ask_someone: Ask a friendly passer-by to stand on the harbour pier looking back at the promenade while you stand on the Riva with the palm row and the palace wall behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The Riva is an open public promenade with no closures known. Respect any signs about photography inside specific attractions such as the Cathedral.
card.challenge: Catch one boat, one palm tree and one stroller in the same frame, then see if you can do it without a stranger blocking the palace wall.
card.good_to_know: The Riva is Split's long, pedestrian waterfront promenade. Guides compare Trg Republike with St Mark's Square in Venice and praise its symmetry. Keep your phone camera clean, because sea air and fingers smudge it quickly.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Start in the middle of Trg Republike, the square at the west end of the Riva, and face into the square so the buildings frame both sides. Then walk the 200 m or so along the promenade, with the Riva to the south-east, and turn back to shoot the palms and palace wall from near the water's edge.

card.hook: Poljud doesn't look like a football ground. It looks like a giant concrete shell that landed in Split, and that bold curved roof does most of the photo work for you.
card.stand_here: The stadium is 109 m to the north-west, so face north-west and you'll have the whole building in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the whole roof in one go. If you're close and it won't fit, switch to 0.5x. Try zoom 2x or 5x (higher zooms depend on your phone) for close-ups of the concrete and the roof edge.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the roof edge up with a horizontal grid line so the curve looks nicely balanced.
card.best_time: Go in the morning or late afternoon, when the softer light is kind to concrete and the shadows under the roof aren't harsh. Match days are busier around the stadium.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera and switch to 0.5x if your phone has it. Hold the phone a bit low and tilt it up so the curved roof sits over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone to stand on the street corner where Ulica Stjepana Radića meets the northern approach road and face south, while you stand between them and the stadium so the full roof curve is behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Drone photography is generally prohibited here, so keep to your phone. Access can change on match days and during building work, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Get the whole roof in one frame with sky filling the top third, then check the edges for lamp posts and parked cars before you tap.
card.good_to_know: Poljud is the home ground of Hajduk Split, designed by architect Boris Magaš. It opened in September 1979, and the roof spans 206 by 47 metres. It now seats 33,987 (down from 55,000) and was officially recognised as cultural heritage in 2015.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head for the phone icon on the map. The stadium is 109 m to the north-west, so face north-west and you'll have the whole building in front of you.

The Nomado and Airial pages are AI-style travel guides, so check the junction on the ground before relying on it.

card.hook: You're standing in a sunken Roman courtyard, and a 57-metre bell tower is peeking over the columns like it knows it's the star of the show. It's the most photographed spot in Diocletian's Palace, and one look tells you why.
card.stand_here: Stand in the Peristil, at the southern end near the Protiron arch, and look north up the colonnade. The bell tower and facade rise above the columns, with the arch and the palace colonnade around them.
card.zoom: Start at 0.5x to squeeze the colonnade, the arch and the tall bell tower into one shot. Then try 1x for a cleaner, less stretched look, and 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) for the top of the tower and the carved details.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the bell tower on one of the vertical lines, and hold your phone level so the tower doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, around 6:30 to 8:00 in summer, when the square is least crowded. If people wander into your shot, wait a moment and take a few frames.
card.selfie_here: Take your selfie in the middle of the Peristyle (Peristil Square), where the bell tower looms above you. Use the front camera, tilt it up a little, and keep the tower over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand in the Peristil square facing the cathedral front, while you stand in front of the cathedral entrance, so the whole bell tower and front fit in the frame.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos inside the cathedral are generally allowed, but be discreet and never use flash, especially during services. It's a working place of worship, so dress modestly and keep your voice down. The bell tower climb needs a head for heights, because the steep stone stairs give way to flimsy metal stairs over the internal void.
card.challenge: Can you get the bell tower perfectly straight between two columns, with nobody's elbow in the corner?
card.good_to_know: The cathedral began life in AD 305 as the mausoleum of the Roman emperor Diocletian, and it's still used as a cathedral today. Its walnut doors were carved in 1214 by Andrija Buvina and show 28 scenes from the life of Christ. Very few medieval wooden doors survive in such good condition.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in the Peristil, at the southern end near the Protiron arch, and look north up the colonnade. The bell tower and facade rise above the columns, with the arch and the palace colonnade around them.

card.hook: Picture a roof with a frog sitting on it, looking very pleased with itself. That's your clue you've found Froggyland, a little Split museum with 507 stuffed frogs doing very human things.
card.stand_here: Stand at the phone icon on the map, right outside Froggyland at Ul. kralja Tomislava 5. Face the front door so the building fills your screen.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the whole front of the building. If the sign and the roof frog won't both fit, try zoom 0.5x.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line up the front door so the building sits nice and level.
card.best_time: Go when it's quieter, so fewer people wander into your frame. Check the official site for visiting times.
card.selfie_here: Stand on the pavement in front of the museum's front door, with the 'Specialty Museum' sign and the roof frog behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x to squeeze it all in, and tilt the phone up a touch so the frog makes it into the shot.
card.rules_and_safety: Photography isn't allowed inside the museum, and postcards are sold instead. Sources disagree on exterior photos, so check on arrival. Some people find the frogs cruel, so be thoughtful about how you share your pictures.
card.challenge: Spot the roof frog before anyone else in your group does, then give it a starring role in your selfie.
card.good_to_know: Froggyland has 21 little scenes with 507 stuffed frogs. Ferenc Mere, born in 1878, prepared them between 1910 and 1920. The collection was found in an attic in Serbia, and in 1970 the current owner's parents brought it to Split.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the phone icon on the map, right outside Froggyland at Ul. kralja Tomislava 5. Face the front door so the building fills your screen.

card.hook: A stone villa with eight bronze figures standing on the lawn out front is a pretty good deal for one photo stop. The sculptor, Ivan Meštrović, designed the house himself, so the building is just as much the star as the statues.
card.stand_here: Head for the Ivan Meštrović Gallery on the Marjan peninsula, where the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Face the villa, then step back within the grounds or park until the whole façade fits comfortably in your shot.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole façade and the sculptures in front of it. Switch to 1x for a more natural look, then try 2x-5x (depending on your phone) for close-ups of a sculpture or the stonework.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines and line up the edges of the villa with the vertical lines so the building doesn't lean.
card.best_time: Go when the light is soft and the façade isn't in harsh glare, like in the morning or later in the afternoon. When you arrive, check which side of the building is lit.
card.selfie_here: Try the garden terraces on the sea-view side. Stand at the terrace edge with the Adriatic in front and the gallery behind you, then use the front camera at 0.5x to squeeze in more of the villa over your shoulder. Another good spot is the grand front staircase, standing between the fountains.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand at the foot of the front stone steps, below the façade, so the whole villa fits in the frame while you pose up by the building.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos for private use are allowed without flash. Professional photography and filming need prior permission from the gallery. The garden has unfenced drops near some terrace edges, so keep children close when posing on the terraces.
card.challenge: Find a bronze figure and frame it so the villa's stone wall sits right behind it, then take one more shot that's all wall and no statue, and see which one you like better.
card.good_to_know: Meštrović designed the villa as a family home, a working studio and a place to show his work. It was built between 1931 and 1939 and looks over the Adriatic. He donated the property to the state in 1952, and the renovated permanent display opened on 18 May 1998.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head for the Ivan Meštrović Gallery on the Marjan peninsula, where the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Face the villa, then step back within the grounds or park until the whole façade fits comfortably in your shot.

card.hook: There's a sphinx from Egypt guarding a Roman temple door in the middle of Split, and almost nobody expects it. Add the carved gods above the doorway and a bell tower on top, and you've got a very crowded little photo.
card.stand_here: Start on the steps at the edge of the Peristil, Diocletian's Palace's central square, a short walk east of the temple. Face the Protyron arch so it frames your shot. The temple isn't in view from here, so this is your wide scene-setter. Then walk west for the entrance.
card.zoom: At the temple entrance, stay at 1x so the sphinx, the doorway and the reliefs all fit. From the Peristil steps, try 2x to pick out the arch and details when the square is busy.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, then tap the temple's stonework and drag the slider down a little to make it darker so the pale stone keeps its detail.
card.best_time: Go early, before 9am. The Peristil is nearly empty and the light is better.
card.selfie_here: Stand beside the headless sphinx at the temple entrance, use the front camera and see what you can fit over your shoulder. For a moodier portrait, try the narrow stone lane that runs from the Peristil to the temple.
card.rules_and_safety: The outside is free to walk around, but going inside needs a paid combined palace ticket, so check the official site first. Photos inside are generally allowed, but look for signs on the day.
card.challenge: Take one shot with the sphinx big in the foreground and the carved gods peeking over its head. Bonus points if no stranger wanders into it.
card.good_to_know: The temple was built between 295 and 305 as part of Diocletian's Palace and dedicated to Jupiter. It was later turned into a baptistery, probably in the 6th century, and the Romanesque bell tower was added in the 11th century. The Scottish architect Robert Adam thought it one of the most beautiful monuments in Europe.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Start on the steps at the edge of the Peristil, Diocletian's Palace's central square, a short walk east of the temple. Face the Protyron arch so it frames your shot. The temple isn't in view from here, so this is your wide scene-setter. Then walk west for the entrance.

card.hook: Meet the biggest bishop in Split: a bronze Gregory of Nin with one arm raised, standing just outside the Golden Gate like he's hailing a taxi. You really can't miss him, and he's very happy to be in your photo.
card.stand_here: Stand near the statue of Gregory of Nin on Kralja Tomislava, right beside the Golden Gate (from the Peristyle, walk north to get there). Step back until the whole figure fits, then face the statue so the gate is behind him.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the full figure with the Golden Gate behind. If you can't step back far enough, drop to 0.5x. For a close-up of the upper body and raised arm against the sky, try 2x, or up to 5x if your phone has it.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines to keep the old walls straight, then tap the statue and slide it a little darker so the bronze keeps its detail and the sky doesn't go white.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, before the tour groups arrive. Midday is the busiest, with crowds from cruise ships, so a clear frame is harder then.
card.selfie_here: Try the half wall below the steps near the statue and the Golden Gate. One reviewer calls it the best place for pictures, but it's not confirmed as a selfie spot, so check the view on the spot. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if you want more in, and keep the statue or the gate over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to step back along the park path in Đardin park next to the statue, so the whole figure and the Golden Gate fit in one frame with you in it.
card.rules_and_safety: The Old Town gets busy near the statue and pickpockets are a concern, so keep your phone and wallet secure.
card.challenge: Get low, aim up, and catch his raised arm against the sky, then see if your friends can guess who he's waving at.
card.good_to_know: The statue is about 7.6 to 8.5 metres tall, and accounts differ on the exact height. It was moved here from the Peristyle in 1954. It stands in the open and is free to visit at any hour.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand near the statue of Gregory of Nin on Kralja Tomislava, right beside the Golden Gate (from the Peristyle, walk north to get there). Step back until the whole figure fits, then face the statue so the gate is behind him.

card.hook: Picture walking under a stone ceiling that once held up an emperor's private apartments. That's the Cellars of Diocletian's Palace, and the arches just keep going.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, in the Cellars of Diocletian's Palace at the southern end of Split's Old Town. Face along the hall so the arches shrink away in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole length of a vaulted hall into one shot. Switch to 1x for the wine press and other details. Use 2x-5x only for far-off arches, and expect a grainier picture if the light is low.
card.make_it_pop: Tap a plain bit of wall, then drag the slider a little darker so any bright doorway doesn't turn into a white blob.
card.best_time: Pick a quiet moment, because fewer people in the frame makes the vaults look far better. The free central passage can get crowded with stalls, and the ticketed eastern and western halls are described as quieter. Check the official site for current visiting times.
card.selfie_here: Go down the stairs at the Brass Gate, turn left into the museum section, and stand in the cellar on the right just after the ticket office. Use the front camera, hold it a bit low and keep the stone vault behind your shoulder. This is said to be the chamber used for the Daenerys dragon scenes, but it comes from just one blog, so double-check it when you're there.
card.rules_and_safety: Photos for personal use are generally allowed, but selfie sticks may have restrictions and flash may be banned. Check the official site for current access and photography rules, and keep your elbows in and give other visitors room.
card.challenge: Try to catch the arches so evenly that the left and right sides look like twins, then see if anyone notices the one wonky step you took to get there.
card.good_to_know: The cellars cover roughly an eighth of the palace's area, and their layout follows the rooms that were above. In Roman times they stored food and wine, and you can still see the remains of a large press. The western halls opened to visitors in 1959 and the eastern part in 1996.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, in the Cellars of Diocletian's Palace at the southern end of Split's Old Town. Face along the hall so the arches shrink away in front of you.

selfie_spots.why: This is the vaulted chamber used for the Daenerys dragon scenes, so the stone cellar sits behind you as the backdrop for a fan-style selfie.

card.hook: Most people hurry through the Golden Gate on the way to lunch. Slow down for ten seconds, because the stonework is the real show: a grand arch, a row of niches and some tiny carved faces peeking down at you.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, on the north side outside the Golden Gate, and face the gate. Keep Meštrović's bronze statue of Bishop Gregory of Nin slightly to one side so it doesn't hide the doorway.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the gate, the statue and the walls in one frame. Switch to 1x for a more natural look, then try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) to home in on the niches, the arch and the little carved faces above the doorway.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines, keep the arch in the middle and hold your phone level so the stone rows stay straight.
card.best_time: Go early, shortly after sunrise, or in the evening when the stone looks warmer. Midday is the busiest time, when tour groups come through.
card.selfie_here: Take your selfie on the open pavement just outside the north arch, beside the Gregory of Nin statue, so the palace wall runs alongside you and the gate stays behind you. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x, and tilt the phone slightly up so the arch sits over your shoulder. For a calmer backdrop, the shaded green space (Đardin park) right beside the gate is another option.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to step back from the statue on the north approach until the statue and the palace entrance both fit in the frame, while you stand next to the statue.
card.challenge: Can you spot all five niches and at least one tiny carved face above the doorway, and get them in the same photo as you?
card.good_to_know: The arch above the opening is made of 19 stone blocks, and the front has five niches and a row of small blind arches. The gate was sealed off in the Middle Ages and lost its columns and statues, then reopened in 1857. It was wrapped for restoration from 2012 until 2015, and two octagonal towers that once flanked it are now gone.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand right at the phone icon on the map, on the north side outside the Golden Gate, and face the gate. Keep Meštrović's bronze statue of Bishop Gregory of Nin slightly to one side so it doesn't hide the doorway.

card.hook: Everyone crowds into the middle of the Peristyle, but the best frame is from the quiet doorway behind them. From there the arch wraps around the columns like a picture frame, and the people living in this old palace carry on behind you.
card.stand_here: Stand at the Vestibul, just inside the archway, and face north. The Peristyle opens out in front of you, framed by the arch, with the colonnade ahead.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x inside the Vestibul to fit in the domed hall and the whole arch. Switch to 1x for a tidier frame around the columns, then try 2x to 5x (higher zooms depend on your phone) to pull in the colonnade and bell tower.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the arch up with the edges so the columns stay upright, then tap the bright courtyard and drag the slider to make it a little darker so the pale stone keeps its detail.
card.best_time: Go when it's least crowded, so nobody walks into your archway view. Some people swear by early morning and others by golden hour, so pick whichever suits your day.
card.selfie_here: On the Peristyle, stand in front of one of the white marble colonnade columns, facing the square. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and tilt up so the columns rise behind your shoulder. The black granite sphinx near the cathedral entrance also makes a fun prop.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand under the open Protiron archway at the southern end of the Peristyle and shoot north up the colonnade toward the cathedral bell tower, while you pose among the columns.
card.rules_and_safety: The polished stone is very slippery when wet, so watch your step while you look at your screen. The cathedral and baptistery are active religious spaces, so follow any posted instructions. Street performers may ask for payment if you photograph them, and bulky selfie sticks don't suit the narrow lanes.
card.challenge: Get one shot where the dark arch makes a perfect border around the bright courtyard and every column stands up straight, like a tiny Roman postcard.
card.good_to_know: Emperor Diocletian had this palace built as his retirement home at the end of the third century AD. Today it makes up about half of Split's old town, around 3,000 people live inside it, and UNESCO listed it as a World Heritage Site in 1979. The cathedral at the far end sits in the building first put up as a temple and later used as Diocletian's Mausoleum, and its Romanesque bell tower was completed between the 12th and 14th centuries.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the Vestibul, just inside the archway, and face north. The Peristyle opens out in front of you, framed by the arch, with the colonnade ahead.

card.hook: Imagine a huge stone oval sitting in open ground, with hills behind it and nothing in the way. That's the Salona amphitheatre, and it's the easiest place on the site to get a big, simple, impressive photo.
card.stand_here: Stand right at the subject, on the south side of the amphitheatre, and look west or east along the outer walls. Keep the curve of the stone in front of you and the hills behind.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole oval and its surroundings in one shot. Switch to 1x for the long lines of the outer walls, then try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the stone tiers and arches without walking onto the uneven ground.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the curve of the walls along the lower line, and keep the phone level so the stones don't lean.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning. The light is kinder and the tour groups haven't arrived yet, so your photos have fewer strangers in them.
card.selfie_here: Walk into the middle of the arena floor, switch to the front camera and use 0.5x so the ruined walls and arches wrap around you. Guides call this the most photogenic ruin at Salona. For a second spot, stand on the stone road in front of Porta Caesarea (Caesar's Gate) with the gate over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the footpath just past the small car park, where the amphitheatre comes into view, while you stand ahead of them with the whole ruin behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The ground is open and uneven, so watch your step while you look at the screen. Keep to the visitor paths, since some gardens nearby are private, and stay out of the taller grass in summer because snakes may be in it. Personal photos are generally fine, but check with the site first if you want to fly a drone.
card.challenge: Take one photo of the whole oval at 0.5x, then one tight shot of just the arches at 2x or more, and see if your friends can tell they're the same place.
card.good_to_know: Salona was one of the largest cities of the late Roman Empire and the capital of the Roman province of Dalmatia. Today it's the largest archaeological park in Croatia. If you have time, the early Christian church ruins at Manastirine are a quieter second stop, with stones and sarcophagi among greenery.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand right at the subject, on the south side of the amphitheatre, and look west or east along the outer walls. Keep the curve of the stone in front of you and the hills behind.

card.hook: Picture a big, butter-yellow theatre filling one whole side of an open square, with plain modern buildings standing around it looking a bit jealous. That's the Croatian National Theatre, and the colour does most of the work for you.
card.stand_here: Stand in Trg Gaje Bulata, once the theatre is to the west, about 1 minute on foot. Face the front of the building so the yellow facade sits in the middle of your photo with open square around it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the whole facade with the square in front. If you're close and it won't fit, drop to 0.5x. For details on the upper facade, try zoom 2x to 5x, depending on your phone.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the yellow wall, then slide the brightness down a little so the yellow stays rich instead of washing out.
card.best_time: Late afternoon or early evening is the sweet spot, when the square is less shaded. The facade looks different by day and by night, so check the light when you arrive.
card.selfie_here: Take your selfie in Trg Gaje Bulata, right in front of the theatre, with the yellow facade behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x so more of the building squeezes in, and keep the facade over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand across the square from the theatre, so they can fit the whole facade and the modern glass mall beside it, while you stand in front of the yellow wall.
card.rules_and_safety: The square is open public space. If you go inside, check the official site first, and note that photography isn't allowed inside during performances.
card.challenge: Take one shot where the yellow is the star and nobody is in it, then one where you're in it grinning. Which one wins?
card.good_to_know: The theatre opened in 1893 as the Split Municipal Theatre, in the time of mayor Gajo Bulat, and was designed by local architects Emilio Vecchietti and Ante Bezić. It held about 1,000 people when Split had only 16,000 residents, which made it the biggest theatre in Southeast Europe at the time. A fire in February 1970 nearly destroyed it, and the rebuilt theatre reopened in May 1980. It's still a working theatre today.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Trg Gaje Bulata, once the theatre is to the west, about 1 minute on foot. Face the front of the building so the yellow facade sits in the middle of your photo with open square around it.

card.hook: Dark pine trunks, a pale cliff edge and open water with islands on the horizon: Sustipan keeps it simple, and that's why it works. Don't grab your first frame. Walk the paths for a bit first.
card.stand_here: Start at the map point in the middle of Sustipan, then take a walk west to the westernmost edge of the park, on the cliff. Turn around and face back along the cliff line, with the pines and sea in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the cliff edge, pines and sea. Try zoom 0.5x if you want more tree line and sky, and zoom 2x-5x (depending on your phone) for the gloriette or the far-off islands.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the cliff edge along the lower third line, then tap the pines and slide the brightness a little darker so the sky and sea keep their colour.
card.best_time: Late afternoon or early evening is a good choice, and the sea looks warmer then. Leave yourself time to get out before the park closes.
card.selfie_here: Climb the steps of the neoclassical gloriette in the middle of the park and turn so it sits behind you. Use the front camera at zoom 0.5x and hold your phone a little low so more of the gloriette fits in.
card.rules_and_safety: The cliffs drop steeply, so keep well back from the edge when you compose your shot, and never step closer for a better angle. The park is described as gated and open during the day only, so check current opening hours before you go.
card.challenge: Take two photos from the same path: one wide shot of the pines and sea, and one close one of just the islands. Which one would you send to a friend?
card.good_to_know: Sustipan is a small green peninsula, about 325 metres across, and the name means Saint Stephen. In the Middle Ages a Benedictine monastery and a church stood here. A well-known cemetery was laid out in the 19th century and removed in the 20th, so now it's pines, paths and sea views.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Start at the map point in the middle of Sustipan, then take a walk west to the westernmost edge of the park, on the cliff. Turn around and face back along the cliff line, with the pines and sea in front of you.

Other Sustipan sources describe cliff-edge sea views and the northern walls, but do not put the park's landmark behind the visitor, so I left them out. card.hook: Picture a 1,700-year-old Roman gateway with fruit and veg stalls for neighbours. That's the Silver Gate, and it's much more fun than its "secondary gate" label suggests.
card.stand_here: Stand in Poljana kraljice Jelene, the open square outside the gate on the Green Market (Pazar) side. Face the palace's east wall, with the arch in the middle of your frame.
card.zoom: Start at 1x and step back until you get the whole arch with both towers. If the square is crowded and you can't back up, switch to 0.5x. Then try 2x or 5x (depending on your phone) for the niches and the stonework.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the arch in the centre and keep the tower edges straight so the walls don't lean.
card.best_time: Early evening is a good bet. Mornings are busier because of the market, so stalls and traffic can sneak into your shot. If that happens, wait a moment for a gap.
card.selfie_here: Stand on the market side of the east wall, facing the stalls, with the arch behind you. Use the front camera (try 0.5x if your phone has it) and tilt it up a little so the arch fits over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand opposite the gate, near the Church of St Catherine of Alexandria, while you stand in front of the arch.
card.rules_and_safety: The gate and the square outside are open to everyone. One guide warns that the white-tiled palace foundation is slippery, so watch your step. Check the official site before you go for the church above the gate or the neighbouring museum.
card.challenge: Spot the two empty niches beside the arch, which probably once held statues, and get a photo where you're striking the same pose.
card.good_to_know: The Silver Gate is the eastern entrance to Diocletian's Palace and one of its four main gates. It's less ornate than the Golden Gate on the north side. A small church to St Apolinar was probably built above it around the 6th century, and the gate was heavily renovated in 1952. Pope John Paul II drove through it in his popemobile in 2000.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Poljana kraljice Jelene, the open square outside the gate on the Green Market (Pazar) side. Face the palace's east wall, with the arch in the middle of your frame.

card.hook: The Iron Gate is easy to walk straight past in the crowds, which is a shame, because there's a whole stack of history squeezed into this one small frame. Roman arch, a clock, and a bell tower, all at once.
card.stand_here: Stand on the west side of Narodni trg (People's Square), facing the gate. You'll see the arched stone front with the medieval clock tower beside it, and the square's buildings around them.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the gate, clock tower and buildings in together. Go to 2x or higher to pick out the clock face. Use 0.5x only up close, like when you're looking up at the arch.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on your gridlines, put the tower on one side and the arch near the centre, and keep the phone level so the buildings don't lean.
card.best_time: Go early or late in the day. The lane is narrow and gets crowded, so you'll get a much clearer view of the gate when it's quieter.
card.selfie_here: Stay on Narodni trg, just outside the gate's western wall, and turn so the gate is behind you. Use the front camera, try 0.5x to squeeze more of the gate in, and let the arch and tower peek over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone to stand on the north side of the square near the Town Hall loggia and shoot back toward the gate and clock tower, while you pose with the gate behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Photography is widely allowed in the open-air palace area. Bulky selfie sticks don't suit the narrow lanes, so keep it simple.
card.challenge: Find the clock and see if you can spot what's odd about it, then get a shot where the arch, clock and bell tower are all in one frame.
card.good_to_know: The Iron Gate is one of the four main Roman gates of Diocletian's Palace, and the only one still in everyday use. The bell tower dates from the 11th century and is described as the oldest preserved bell tower on the Adriatic coast. The clock shows 24 hours instead of 12, and a small church was built above the gate in the 6th century.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the west side of Narodni trg (People's Square), facing the gate. You'll see the arched stone front with the medieval clock tower beside it, and the square's buildings around them.
